attributes.board_name: North Dakota Board of Physical Therapy

rules.accepted_credit_types: One unit = one hour of participation. Activities related to physical therapy approved by APTA, state PT associations or state PT boards; APTA specialty certification/recertification = 15 units; PT residency program = 25 units; clinical instruction 1 unit per 165 hours (max 5 per period); teaching an approved activity with preparation credit up to 5:1 (one course per year); teaching in an accredited PT/PTA program (not primary occupation) 1 unit per contact hour, max 5. No credit for orientation, meals, keynotes, offices/delegate service or non-educational meetings.
rules.new_licensee_rule: Licensees coming from other states or countries without 25 units in the last two years must complete 13 units within a year of initial North Dakota licensure, then join the two-year cycle.
rules.audit_note: Attestation at the January license renewal deadline following the two-year cycle; the Board audits a 10% sample of licensees each year (documentation from the licensee or from state/national record-keeping organizations).
rules.notes: No mandatory topics. 25 units per two-year continuing competence cycle; the Board sets the reporting groups and deadlines; attestation is due at the January renewal deadline after the cycle. The Board website did not respond on 2026-11-25; figures are taken from the administrative code.
